requested_parts: In a four-player standard game, how many Escape Pods are selected, how are they distributed and oriented, and which tokens start in the Intruder bag?
answers.answer: 1) Four players select 3 random Pods; place the lowest in A, next in B, then alternate A/B, all Locked-side up. 2) Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total).
answers.evidence: “3 pods for 3–4 players”; “All pods start with their Locked side face up”; “1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player.”

requested_parts: How are Objectives filtered and dealt, when does each player choose one, what happens to the rejected card, and do Eggs trigger that choice?
answers.answer: 1) Remove objectives marked for a higher player count, shuffle Personal and Corporate separately, then deal one of each to each player. 2) Players receive them before character draft and choose one of the two at the first Intruder appearance, removing the rejected card face down unseen; Eggs do not trigger this because they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: “Remove from both Objective decks ... all cards showing a player count higher”; “deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective”; “first time an Intruder miniature ... appears”; “Eggs are not Intruders.”

requested_parts: You use an Action card with printed cost 2 while holding that card, two other Action cards and two Contamination cards. What is discarded, and can Contamination substitute for payment? What if the card offers OR effects?
answers.answer: 1) Discard the used Action card plus two additional Action cards (three Action cards total); two Contamination cards cannot pay. 2) If the card has OR sections, choose one.
answers.evidence: “discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards”; “Contamination cards ... can never be discarded to pay any Action cost”; “If a card has two sections separated by ‘OR,’ choose one.”

requested_parts: A Character in a burning Room takes one Action then passes. When do they take Fire damage, can they act again this Player Phase, can they discard cards, and do later players rounds burn them again?
answers.answer: 1) After completing their one-Action round and passing, take one Light Wound at the end of that round. 2) They cannot take later normal Actions that Player Phase, but may discard any number of hand cards when passing. 3) Later players’ rounds do not cause another Fire wound to this Character that turn.
answers.evidence: “ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound”; “passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn”; “At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards.”

requested_parts: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?
answers.answer: 1) Reveal the tile, resolve its face-down Exploration token, orient tile so its token number faces the printed Item Counter, and remove token to box. 2) Resolve effect, then ordinary Movement Noise only if destination empty; place a number result in that Corridor, with existing noise causing Encounter. 3) Silence/Danger replace roll; an occupied destination skips it. Danger moves all eligible adjacent Intruders, or puts noise in every unmarked connected corridor if none.
answers.evidence: “flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token”; “rotate the Room tile until the token’s number faces the Item Counter”; “return that token to the box”; “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll”; “If anyone ... is already there, do NOT roll.”

requested_parts: What does Careful Movement cost and replace, when is it forbidden, and can a Closed Door be crossed or a miniature stop in a Corridor?
answers.answer: 1) Careful Movement costs 2 cards and replaces the Noise roll with a Noise marker chosen in a Corridor connected to destination; it also overrides automatic Silence/Danger. 2) Forbidden in Combat or if every destination-connected Corridor already has Noise. 3) Closed Doors block crossing and no miniature may stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: “Careful Movement (cost 2)”; “instead of a Noise roll ... place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor”; “cannot use it while in Combat”; “Closed Door blocks ... Movement”; “no one may ever stop in a Corridor.”

requested_parts: You roll a number for a Corridor already holding Noise, with a Technical Corridors Entrance in your Room. Give the Encounter sequence, Noise removal, token destination and Surprise Attack comparison; do Contamination cards count?
answers.answer: 1) Clear all noise from connected Corridors including Technical Corridors, draw and place a token’s Intruder, then compare its number with triggering player’s hand; fewer cards means Surprise Attack. 2) An existing marker on the rolled corridor resolves Encounter instead of placing another; Technical space is shared by every entrance. 3) Both Action and Contamination cards count for Surprise comparison.
answers.evidence: “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there’s an Entrance)”; “Compare the token’s number to ... hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count)”; “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker”; “treated as if it were in every Technical Corridors Entrance.”

requested_parts: How does Danger resolve with several eligible neighboring Intruders, and when none are eligible? Does moving an Intruder into your Room count as an Encounter? How does Slime affect Silence?
answers.answer: 1) Danger moves ALL adjacent Intruders that are not in Combat with a Character; if none qualify, mark every unmarked connected Corridor, including Technical Corridors when there is an Entrance. 2) Intruder movement into a Character’s Room is not an Encounter. 3) Slime changes Silence to Danger.
answers.evidence: “move ALL eligible Intruders”; “If there are none ... place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected”; “An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter”; “every ‘Silence’ result ... becomes ‘Danger.’”

requested_parts: During an Encounter you draw Blank. What happens to Noise and the Blank; when is an Adult added? Contrast Blank in bag development.
answers.answer: 1) Encounter Blank places noise in each connected Corridor, returns Blank to bag and ends Encounter without miniature; if it was last token add Adult if available. 2) In bag development Blank adds an Adult if available and is returned to bag.
answers.evidence: “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected”; “If the Blank was the LAST token ... add 1 Adult”; “Return the Blank token to the bag”; “Blank — add 1 Adult ... Return the Blank token to the bag.”

requested_parts: Two Intruders attempt to move together from the same Room through one Closed Door. Where do they end, what happens to the Door, can it later close, and would a Noise-triggered appearance be blocked by that Door?
answers.answer: 1) Both Intruders remain in their original Room and simultaneously destroy the Closed Door. 2) A destroyed Door cannot be closed again (unless Plasma Torch). 3) Noise-triggered Intruder appearance ignores a Closed Door.
answers.evidence: “several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put”; “Destroyed ... can never be Closed again (only exception: the Plasma Torch Item)”; “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”

requested_parts: An injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors with Noise already there. What happens to its miniature, injuries, token and Noise? Can Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors?
answers.answer: 1) On entering Technical Corridors the miniature is removed, all Injury markers discarded, and token returned to bag; existing noise on Technical Corridors remains. 2) Characters normally cannot use the ducts; Doors cannot be placed there.
answers.evidence: “discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature”; “A Noise marker ... is NOT removed”; “Characters can never use them”; “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Describe an ordinary Shoot versus Melee Action: card/ammo costs, target location, Contamination, a miss, and the two-hit die result.
answers.answer: 1) Shoot costs one Action card and one Ammo, targets an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in Hand; roll Combat die. 2) Melee costs one Action card, draws one Contamination onto Action discard before rolling, targets Intruder in your Room; miss causes one Serious Wound and double-hit is only one Injury. 3) Shoot double-hit normally gives two Injuries.
answers.evidence: “Shoot (cost 1)”; “discard 1 Ammo”; “Melee Attack (cost 1)”; “draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile”; “any miss also inflicts 1 Serious Wound”; “2-Injury result deals only 1 Injury.”

requested_parts: After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?
answers.answer: 1) Larva dies at 1 Injury; Adult draws one Attack card and dies if blood value is no greater than total injuries; Queen draws two and dies if summed blood is no greater. 2) Dead Adult/Queen places Carcass in Room; Larva does not. 3) Any Retreat arrow replaces numerical check with retreat via Corridor on a drawn Event card; Queen retreats if either card has arrow.
answers.evidence: “Larva ... 1 Injury kills”; “Adult ... Blood ≤ Injuries kills”; “Queen ... Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values”; “Larva ... no Carcass”; “Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER ... shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?
answers.answer: 1) Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder, starting largest (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva); Escape attacks target the escaper. 2) If dead, Corpse remains in starting Room. 3) If survive, move to neighboring unexplored Room, reveal/resolve exploration and make Noise roll if destination empty.
answers.evidence: “BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder ... starting with the larger ones”; “an Escape attack targets the escaper”; “If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room”; “If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored).”

requested_parts: In an ordinary Intruder Attack with several Characters, how is the target chosen and ties broken; how is a hit determined; what changes for Larva and where does its Contamination go?
answers.answer: 1) Target Character with fewest Action cards in hand; tie goes to First Player or next in turn order. 2) Matching Intruder symbol on attack card is hit, otherwise miss. 3) Larva draws no Attack card: it moves to target board and target gets Contamination; if target already has Larva, attacker disappears and existing Larva remains, target still gets card and does not automatically die. Card goes atop Action discard.
answers.evidence: “FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order)”; “matching ... symbol ... resolve ... otherwise ... misses”; “Larva exception: draw no Attack card”; “place it on top of their Action discard pile”; “does not automatically kill them.”

requested_parts: At three Serious Wounds, does dressing one prevent death from a Light Wound? What happens at a third Light Wound otherwise, what does Heal remove, and where do a dead Characters Corpse and Heavy Objects go?
answers.answer: 1) Dressing only suppresses effect; at 3 Serious Wounds any further Wound still kills. 2) A third Light Wound clears Light track and becomes Serious Wound; Heal removes a Light Wound or a Dressed Serious Wound, not an undressed one. 3) Death leaves Corpse Object in Room and drops Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: “Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds”; “on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound”; “Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound”; “drop all their Heavy Objects there.”

requested_parts: Contrast Canteen/Shower scanning with Surgery: which cards are scanned and removed, how is a Larva handled, and what costs or turn consequences follow Surgery?
answers.answer: 1) Canteen/Shower scan only Contamination in hand, remove non-Infected; Infected stays and puts Larva, or kills if a Larva already present (Creeper in Room). Canteen heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes Slime. 2) Surgery scans hand, deck and discard, removes infected cards and Larva if present, then causes 1 Light Wound, automatic pass, shuffles all cards including whole hand, leaving hand empty to next turn.
answers.evidence: “Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND”; “remove all non-Infected ones”; “Infected result places a Larva”; “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard)”; “Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass.”

requested_parts: How can uncarried Eggs be destroyed with Shoot/Melee, grenades, Molotov and Fire; which Melee penalties are waived, when is Noise rolled and when is the Nest destroyed?
answers.answer: 1) Each Injury from Shoot/Melee destroys an uncarried Egg; Grenade destroys 2; Molotov destroys 1 immediately and Fire continues destroying Eggs each Event Fire step (normally 1). 2) Successful Egg Melee retains Contamination draw; missed Egg Melee waives Contamination and Wound, but draw timing is unresolved. 3) Roll Noise after every attempt including miss; remote Grenade/Molotov roll in own Room. Nest destroyed when no Eggs remain; mark with one Injury.
answers.evidence: “Each Injury destroys 1 Egg”; “Grenade ... 2 Eggs”; “Molotov ... 1 Egg immediately”; “A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound”; “after every single ... attempt ... perform a Noise roll”; “When no Eggs remain ... the Nest is destroyed.”

requested_parts: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?
answers.answer: 1) To enter, pay 2 cards for appropriate Evacuation Section action; Pod must be unlocked, have space, and section have no Intruder or Malfunction. Roll Noise first; if Intruder appears/is present, entry fails. 2) Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not take Character space. 3) Waiting passes current turn; at start of first round in each later Player Phase choose stay/pass, launch, or exit free and take 2 Actions. Waiting Character counts present for bag-development Noise; an Intruder appearing ejects occupants to Section Room.
answers.evidence: “pay 2 Action cards”; “Unlocked with a free Character space”; “No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction”; “First roll Noise”; “2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space”; “remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit for free.”

requested_parts: Give the endgame checks in order. What happens with two Damaged Engines, a non-Earth destination (including Quarantine/Mars), and an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva? Do pod passengers need Contamination checks?
answers.answer: 1) Checks: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. 2) Two or more Damaged Engines explode ship and kill all aboard including sleepers; non-Earth destination kills hibernating characters except Quarantine Objective at Mars. 3) Every survivor including Pod passengers gets Contamination check: scan all zones if no Larva; if no Infected there is no four-card draw. With Infected or Larva shuffle all Action/Contamination cards and draw 4; any card kills. Pod passengers still checked.
answers.evidence: “Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives”; “2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode”; “Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters”; “Quarantine Objective survives if ... Mars”; “every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers”; “If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw.”

requested_parts: How are the basic and additional Room tiles and Exploration tokens placed at setup; what Coordinates, Destination, Time, Engines, Eggs and Weaknesses start on the board?
answers.answer: 1) Basic-side board; randomly face-down shuffle tile-2 tiles onto all 2 slots, return extras unseen; place all tile-1 similarly; shuffle Exploration tokens and place one face down each tile, return extras. 2) One random Coordinates face down by Cockpit; Destination at B, Time on green. Engines each have one Working and one Damaged token shuffled face-down in stack. Intruder board starts 5 Eggs and 3 random face-down Weaknesses.
answers.evidence: “Place the board with the basic side up”; “randomly place one face down on each Room slot marked ‘2’”; “Place 1 random Coordinates card”; “Destination marker” on B; “Time marker” green; “5 Egg tokens and 3 random Weakness cards.”

requested_parts: How are Player Numbers assigned and Characters drafted; what does each Character receive and where do Characters and the initial Corpse begin? Are Quest Items usable immediately?
answers.answer: 1) Help card number is Player Number and sets draft order; each drafts from two publicly revealed choices in order. 2) Each takes board, miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10-card Action deck, starting weapon with capacity Ammo, and two inactive horizontal Quest Items. Blue Character Corpse starts Hibernatorium. Quest Items unlock only via mini-quest, not immediately usable.
answers.evidence: “number on the Help card and Inventory is the Player Number”; “Player 1 draws 2 and reveals both choices publicly”; “miniature ... placed in the Hibernatorium”; “Starting Item ... loaded ... equal to ... Ammo capacity”; “2 Quest Items ... NOT active at the start”; “blue Character Corpse token in the Hibernatorium.”

requested_parts: When are Action hands refilled and the First Player token passed; what happens when the Action deck empties, and what are the normal discard destinations and visibility?
answers.answer: 1) At start of Player Phase each draws up to 5; pass First Player token left after draw except first turn. Empty deck: shuffle discard into new deck and draw. 2) Action discards face-up in personal Action discard; Contamination on top of it; normal card discards face up, Item discards to matching pile. Inventory Items remain hidden; used card is shown.
answers.evidence: “every player draws ... up to a hand of 5”; “pass the token to the player on the left (do NOT pass it on the first turn)”; “shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck”; “Normal card discards are face up”; “Gained Contamination cards on top”; “Any Item used must be shown.”

requested_parts: Give the Event Phase order, which Intruders move on an Event card, what controls movement and when the event effect resolves; what happens when Event and Intruder Attack decks run out?
answers.answer: 1) Time and active Self-Destruct advance; Intruder Attacks; Fire Damage and Injury checks; Event movement then event effect; bag development. 2) Only symbol-matching Intruders not in Rooms with Characters move; event number gives Corridor. Technical Corridor result removes miniature and returns token to bag. Event deck reshuffles discards when empty; Intruder Attack deck reshuffles its discard when needed.
answers.evidence: “advance Time”; “Intruder Attack”; “Fire Damage”; “resolve 1 Event card”; “not in a Room with any Characters move ... Corridor matching the number”; “If ... Technical Corridor ... token back in ... bag”; “shuffle the Event discards into a new deck”; “if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile.”

requested_parts: In bag development, describe Larva, Creeper, Adult, Breeder and both Queen branches. Which tokens are removed or returned, who rolls Noise and when does the next turn begin?
answers.answer: 1) Larva removed from bag, add Adult; Creeper removed, add Breeder. Adult returned immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Combat; Breeder causes same rolls then returns. 2) Queen in Nest with characters appears and Encounter; otherwise add Egg; return Queen. 3) Noise from adult/breeder triggers Encounters; turn ends only after entire bag development and resulting Encounters resolve.
answers.evidence: “Larva — remove this token from the bag; add 1 Adult”; “Creeper — remove ... add 1 Breeder”; “Adult ... return ... immediately before ... roll for Noise”; “Breeder ... roll ... then return”; “If any Characters are in the Nest ... Encounter. If no Characters ... add 1 Egg”; “turn only ends once the bag development step is fully resolved.”

requested_parts: When do Fire and Malfunction exhaustion end the game; what if the target Room already has that marker, and where do removed markers go? What happens to sleepers and Intruders when hull integrity is lost?
answers.answer: 1) If asked to place a ninth Fire or Malfunction marker, ship explodes/loses hull and game ends; at most one marker per Room and extra placement on already marked Room does nothing. Removed markers return to supply. 2) Ship destruction kills all on-board Characters including sleepers and all Intruders.
answers.evidence: “if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, the ship explodes and the game ends”; “Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing)”; “discarded markers return to the pool”; “ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders.”

requested_parts: What does a Malfunction disable and leave usable, where can it never be placed, and does it change an Engine token or harm an already-hibernating Character?
answers.answer: 1) Malfunction disables that Room’s Action and Computer; Searching still works. 2) Never place in Nest or Room Covered In Slime; cannot place in unexplored Rooms. 3) Does not alter Engine status; later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not harm/wake sleepers.
answers.evidence: “Room’s Action is unavailable (Searching still works)”; “A Malfunction makes a Room’s Computer unavailable”; “Never placed in the Nest or the Room Covered In Slime”; “cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms”; “Engine status is never affected”; “doesn’t affect already-hibernated Characters.”

requested_parts: Which Items may be hidden, what do other players see, what is the Inventory limit, and what must happen on use? How are Heavy Items/Objects, added Items and Duct Tape handled?
answers.answer: 1) Normal Item cards hidden in holder; others see backs/colors; no Inventory size limit; show any Item when used. 2) Heavy Items/Objects are visible and occupy one of two Hand slots; max two, drop before taking third. Heavy Items found by Search loaded with 1 Ammo; added Items attach and act as one; Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items, not Objects.
answers.evidence: “keeps non-Heavy Item cards hidden”; “others see only card backs/colors”; “No Inventory size limit”; “Any Item used must be shown”; “must occupy one of your 2 Hand slots”; “Weapons found by Searching come loaded with 1 Ammo”; “Duct Tape combines 2 Heavy ITEMS ... (never Objects).”

requested_parts: What happens to an Item versus an Object voluntarily dropped, when and at what Action cost may you drop, and how do found Weapons differ from starting Weapons in Ammo?
answers.answer: 1) Drop is free anytime during your turn: dropped Objects stay in Room; Item cards are lost/discarded. 2) No separate Action cost. 3) Searched Weapons have 1 Ammo; starting Weapon has Ammo equal to capacity.
answers.evidence: “Drop: free, any time during your turn, no Action”; “Dropped Objects stay in the Room; dropped Items are lost (discarded)”; “Starting Item ... loaded ... equal to ... capacity”; “Weapons found by Searching come loaded with 1 Ammo.”

requested_parts: How does Search choose its deck, draw and keep cards, return the rejected card, change the Item Counter, and handle zero Items, Special Rooms and Blue Items?
answers.answer: 1) Search Action uses deck matching Room color; white Room permits any Red/Yellow/Green. Draw 2, keep 1, return rejected face down to bottom of that deck; decrement Item Counter by 1. 2) At zero ordinarily cannot Search; Special Rooms have no Searching; Nest and Slime Room expressly prohibit it. Blue Craft deck is never searched.
answers.evidence: “draws 2 cards from one deck, keeps 1 ... other face down at the bottom”; “Each Search lowers ... Item Counter by 1; at 0 ... cannot be searched”; “Special Rooms ... no Searching”; “Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit”; “Blue (Crafted, never found by searching).”

requested_parts: How does Craft pay its Action and components, must the result be available, can you inspect the deck, and what Crafted Items exist?
answers.answer: 1) Craft is Basic Action costing 1 Action card; discard two Item cards with blue component icons matching result’s two gray icons. 2) Result must be available; deck may be inspected at any time. 3) Crafted items: Antidote, Taser, Flamethrower, Molotov Cocktail; components flame+cross, battery+tool, flame+tool, flame+fabric respectively.
answers.evidence: “Craft Item Basic Action”; “discard 2 Item cards showing ... blue Craft ... icons”; “cannot be built if its card is not available”; “may look through the Craft deck at any time”; “four Crafted Items ... Antidote ... Taser ... Flamethrower ... Molotov Cocktail.”

requested_parts: Who pays for a Trade and who may join; can you give something for nothing, exchange Ammo, or need a separate Pick Up Action for a searched Heavy Item?
answers.answer: 1) Only trade initiator pays one Action card; all Characters in Room may join and exchanges require agreement. 2) Giving Item/Object for nothing is allowed; Ammo cannot be exchanged. 3) A searched Heavy Item is already acquired by Search, requiring no separate Pick Up Action (Pick Up applies to Objects).
answers.evidence: “Only the initiator spends the Action”; “trade with all Characters in your Room”; “You may give ... for nothing”; “Characters cannot exchange Ammo”; “Heavy Items found by Searching do not require this Action.”

requested_parts: How do you reveal Weaknesses: what Object corresponds to each card, where must it be, is it consumed, who benefits and must you personally research for a Discover Weakness Objective?
answers.answer: 1) Research matching Object: Character Corpse, Egg or Intruder Carcass in Laboratory; reveal corresponding Weakness, leave face up, not consumed; benefit applies to all players. 2) Discover Weakness Objective is fulfilled if anyone researches it before game end.
answers.evidence: “Analyse 1 Object (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Egg present in the Room)”; “reveal ... Weakness card face up and leave it”; “Object is not consumed”; “rule benefits all players”; “by anyone before game end.”

requested_parts: What are the common prerequisites and cost for Room Actions, what does a Computer icon itself do, and how does Fire affect Room Actions or Searching?
answers.answer: 1) Room Action requires being in that Room, outside Combat, no Malfunction, and costs 2 Action cards (unless explicit special ability allows otherwise). 2) Computer icon itself has no effect; it marks Computer availability for specific effects. 3) Fire does not stop Room Actions or Search; a player ending own round there takes Light Wound.
answers.evidence: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use”; “cannot ... while in Combat or ... Malfunction”; “Cost: 2 Action cards”; “Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms”; “ending their round ... suffers 1 Light Wound.”

requested_parts: What exactly does the Armory recharge, by how much, and what limits apply?
answers.answer: 1) Armory adds 2 Ammo to one of your Energy Weapons, never Classic Weapons, and cannot exceed capacity.
answers.evidence: “add 2 Ammo to 1 of your Energy Weapons (never Classic Weapons; never above capacity).”

requested_parts: What are the three mutually exclusive Emergency Room treatments; does dressing remove the Wound or merely its effect, and do identical Serious Wound effects stack?
answers.answer: 1) Choose one: Dress all Serious Wounds; Heal one Dressed Serious Wound; or Heal all Light Wounds. 2) Dressing flips card face down and suppresses effect but wound remains; duplicate Serious Wound effects do not stack.
answers.evidence: “Dress ALL your Serious Wounds OR Heal 1 Dressed Serious Wound OR Heal all your Light Wounds”; “effect is ignored, but it still counts”; “Duplicate Serious Wound cards are NOT cumulative.”

requested_parts: What does sending a Signal actually do and what is its game use; can Comms be absent from a normal game?
answers.answer: 1) Send Signal places a Status marker on your Character board’s Signal space, used only for Objectives. 2) Comms Room is always aboard in standard game.
answers.evidence: “Send a Signal: place a Status marker on your board’s Signal space (only used for Objectives)”; “a Comms Room is always aboard.”

requested_parts: How does Fire Control affect a chosen Room and its Intruders if the Room has Fire, or has none?
answers.answer: 1) Choose any one Room, discard its Fire marker if present, and all Intruders there retreat in random directions, drawing one Event card per Intruder. 2) It works even if target Room had no Fire, still scattering Intruders.
answers.evidence: “choose any 1 Room: discard its Fire marker (if any) and ALL Intruders there run away in random directions”; “Works even with no Fire.”

requested_parts: Describe starting, stopping and restarting Self-Destruct, advancing it, the yellow threshold, its final space, a jump while active and a Character already hibernating.
answers.answer: 1) Start at green space; advances one space whenever Time advances. Any Character may stop/remove marker, which restarts from green if started again. 2) First yellow is unabortable and unlocks all Pods; later yellow spaces do not unlock again though Pods may be relocked. Skull space explodes ship. 3) Character cannot start while anyone hibernates; Coolant Leak Event can. Jump while active still counts ship destroyed.
answers.evidence: “marker advances 1 space every time the Time marker advances”; “Any Character stopping ... removes the marker”; “first yellow ... can no longer be aborted”; “subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again”; “final (‘skull’) space ... explodes”; “Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers”; “ship is still considered destroyed.”

requested_parts: Which Room can Airlock Control target, what Door condition is required, what happens immediately, and what cancels or completes the procedure and when?
answers.answer: 1) Target any one OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors have no Destroyed Door. Close every Door around it and place procedure token immediately. 2) If all Doors remain closed at end of current Player Phase, everything there dies and Fire removed; opening any Door first cancels.
answers.evidence: “pick any 1 OTHER Yellow Room whose connected Corridors contain no Destroyed Doors”; “automatically Close every Door around it”; “when the current Player Phase ends”; “If any ... Door is opened first, the procedure is cancelled.”

requested_parts: When does Cabins increase a hand and to what size; what disables it and is it a paid Room Action?
answers.answer: 1) At start of new turn, Character in Cabins with no Intruder present draws one extra card, hand size 6. 2) Malfunction disables it; passive, not paid Room Action.
answers.evidence: “at the start of a new turn”; “hand of 6 instead of 5”; “Disabled by a Malfunction token.”

requested_parts: Can Command Center select a distant Room and individually open some Doors and close others, including a Destroyed Door?
answers.answer: 1) Command Center selects any Room, including distant, and may open/close any chosen subset of Doors in its connected Corridors. Destroyed Doors can never be closed except Plasma Torch, so Command Center cannot close them.
answers.evidence: “choose any 1 Room and Open/Close any of the Doors in its connected Corridors (your choice which)”; “Destroyed ... can never be Closed again (only exception: Plasma Torch).”

requested_parts: What can Engine Control Room check or change and how do Malfunctions in an Engine Room affect that check?
answers.answer: 1) Engine Control Room checks status of all 3 Engines but cannot change it. Malfunction in an Engine Room does not stop this check. 2) Changes are by Repairs Action/Tools while in the Engine Room; those work despite a Room Malfunction.
answers.evidence: “check the status of all 3 Engines (works even if an Engine Room has a Malfunction marker; you cannot CHANGE Engine status here)”; “Repair/Break Engine ... Works even with a Malfunction marker.”

requested_parts: What does Hatch Control System change and how does Monitoring Room inspect a location: explored or unexplored, what components, secrecy and replacement?
answers.answer: 1) Hatch Control flips one Pod Locked/Unlocked. 2) Monitoring Room secretly examines any one unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replaces them; may lie. Nemesis Plans differs: can privately check 2 tiles, no tokens.
answers.evidence: “flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked”; “secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie)”; “Nemesis Plans ... any 2 ... Do not inspect their Exploration tokens.”

requested_parts: Does entering Room Covered With Slime require an Action to acquire Slime, can it have an Item Counter or Malfunction, can Slime stack, and does showering extinguish Fire?
answers.answer: 1) Slime is gained automatically on entry, no Action. 2) No Item count is set; Malfunction cannot be placed; Slime max one and further has no effect. 3) Shower removes Slime but does not remove Fire.
answers.evidence: “entering automatically gives you a Slime marker”; “no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here”; “Max 1 (further Slime does nothing)”; “Fire ... is NOT removed by showering.”

requested_parts: In Cockpit what can you learn or change, who sees the information, what does Destination refer to and which restrictions apply after someone hibernates or an Intruder is present?
answers.answer: 1) Cockpit lets you secretly check Coordinates and replace/remember it, or set Destination by moving marker; you may lie about Coordinates. Marker picks one of four entries on Coordinates card. 2) Cannot set with Intruder in Cockpit or change Destination once anyone hibernates.
answers.evidence: “Check Coordinates (secretly look ... you may lie; replace it and remember it) OR Set Destination”; “marker selects one of the four destination entries”; “never Set Destination with an Intruder”; “or change Destination once anyone is hibernating.”

requested_parts: How does Engine checking differ from repairing/breaking; what can stay secret, what must be announced and do you need a prior check or functioning Engine Room?
answers.answer: 1) Checking Engine secretly inspect top token and may lie. Repair/Break secretly examine both tokens and restack in any order; need not disclose if repaired, but must say if order changed. 2) Works with Malfunction and without prior check; Engine Control Room only checks.
answers.evidence: “Check the Engine (secretly look at the TOP token; you may lie)”; “secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order”; “needn’t say whether you repaired it, but you MUST say if you changed the order”; “Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first.”

requested_parts: When is hibernation legal, what roll and failure condition apply, what leaves play on success, and which later ship actions are forbidden? Does later Malfunction wake sleepers?
answers.answer: 1) Hibernation requires Time on blue space, presence in Hibernatorium, 2 cards, no Intruder or Malfunction; roll Noise, and an Intruder appearing/reaching makes failure. Success removes mini and ends participation until end checks. 2) Once anyone hibernates no Character can change Destination or start Self-Destruct; later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleeper.
answers.evidence: “pay 2 Action cards while present, with Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction”; “Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing ... makes ... fail”; “remove your miniature and stop participating”; “no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct”; “later ... Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers.”

requested_parts: What ends the game when Time runs out or the last active Character leaves/dies/hibernates; how is an active Self-Destruct resolved and do Intruders die from a normal jump?
answers.answer: 1) Time final red space causes immediate jump; awake aboard Characters die, Intruders survive. Ship destruction (Self-Destruct final or ninth Fire/Malfunction) kills everyone and Intruders. 2) Last living awake Character leaving by death, hibernating or Pod launch triggers immediate final-time or active Self-Destruct result. 3) Normal jump does not kill Intruders.
answers.evidence: “Time marker reaches the final red space ... jumps ... every Character ... not hibernating dies”; “Intruders are unharmed”; “ship explodes ... ALL Characters ... and everything else aboard dies”; “last ... dies, hibernates, or launches”; “move ... to its final red space.”

requested_parts: Can a Character directly attack another, and may an Action still harm other crew indirectly? Give source-supported examples.
answers.answer: 1) Characters cannot directly attack other Characters. 2) Indirect harm is possible, e.g. lock someone in burning Room, activate Self-Destruct with crew aboard, or throw Grenade into Room with crew.
answers.evidence: “Characters can never directly attack other Characters”; “harm them indirectly: locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct ... throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew.”

requested_parts: You must place an Adult but all eight models are on board. What explicit procedure applies, and what if an Intruder enters an unexplored Room by movement?
answers.answer: 1) If Adult model overflow, remove all Adults not in Combat, return their tokens to bag if possible, then place Adult in Encounter Room. If all eight Adults are in Combat, summary explicitly says procedure unresolved. 2) Intruder entering unexplored Room does not reveal Room or Exploration token.
answers.evidence: “Adults retreat — remove all Adult models NOT in Combat and return their tokens to the bag ... then place”; “If all 8 Adults are in Combat ... authoritative clarification is needed”; “do not ... reveal the Room or its Exploration token.”

requested_parts: For shooting, describe the target-size restrictions of the small curled and larger curved Intruder die symbols; what happens on those same symbols in Melee against an ineligible target?
answers.answer: 1) Small curled symbol hits Larva/Creeper only; larger curved hits Larva/Creeper/Adult. Ineligible Shoot target is a miss. 2) In Melee same restrictions; ineligible target is a miss and causes your Serious Wound. Summary does not separately explain any additional consequence for these exact die faces beyond normal melee miss.
answers.evidence: “Small curled Intruder symbol ... 1 Injury to Larva/Creeper; miss against other types”; “Larger curved ... Larva/Creeper/Adult; miss against Breeder/Queen”; “Melee ... Same target restriction ... ineligible target means miss and 1 Serious Wound.”

requested_parts: At the final Contamination check, a survivor has no Larva and every Contamination card scans non-Infected. Must they perform the four-card draw or remove those cards, and does an earlier launched Pod escape the Objective check?
answers.answer: 1) With no Larva, scan every Contamination card in deck, hand and discard; if all are non-Infected, no four-card draw and cards are not removed. 2) Launched Pod passengers still undergo final Contamination and Objective checks.
answers.evidence: “If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw”; “This endgame procedure does not remove cards merely because they scanned non-Infected”; “including launched Pod passengers”; “They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks.”

requested_parts: Which two component symbols are required for each Crafted Item: Antidote, Taser, Flamethrower and Molotov Cocktail? Describe the symbols rather than guessing Item-card names.
answers.answer: 1) Antidote: flame + medical cross. 2) Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3) Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool. 4) Molotov: flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: “Antidote = flame + medical cross; Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric.”

requested_parts: What defines being in Combat, how do In Combat Only and Out of Combat Only restrictions work, and may an unmarked Action or Item be used in either situation? Do Eggs cause Combat?
answers.answer: 1) Combat means Intruder in your Room; Eggs do not count. In Combat Only requires Intruder present; Out of Combat Only requires none; unmarked Item/card may be used either state subject to requirements. 2) Basic Combat Actions restricted to Shoot, Melee, Escape Movement; Room Actions forbidden.
answers.evidence: “in Combat whenever an Intruder is in your Room. Eggs do not count”; “In Combat only ... only while an Intruder is in your Room”; “No Combat marking ... either situation”; “Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape.”

requested_parts: For an Objective that Player X cannot survive, must you personally kill them, does hibernating or escaping count as death, and how does only survivor differ? What must your own Character do regardless?
answers.answer: 1) For “Player X cannot survive,” X must be dead at end; you need not kill them personally. Hibernating/escaping are surviving, not death. 2) “Only survivor” means nobody else survives. Your own Character must survive and fulfill their Objective regardless.
answers.evidence: “that Character must simply be dead ... (not hibernated, not escaped); you don’t have to kill them”; “no other Character may survive”; “Regardless of Objective, your Character must survive”; “wins if ... fulfill their Objective and survive.”

requested_parts: If a Door token must be placed and none are in the pool, what happens? How are Open, Closed and Destroyed Doors represented, and may two Door tokens share one Corridor or be placed in Technical Corridors?
answers.answer: 1) If Door pool empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on board. 2) Open = no token; Closed = standing token; Destroyed = lying token and cannot be closed again except Plasma Torch. 3) At most one per Corridor; never in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: “If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere”; “Open = no token”; “Closed = standing token”; “Destroyed = lying token”; “max 1 per Corridor”; “never ... in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: The first Character dies while the ship's Pods are Locked. What happens to every Pod immediately, and can they subsequently be Locked again?
answers.answer: 1) First Character death automatically unlocks all Escape Pods immediately. 2) They may later be locked/unlocked normally, e.g. Hatch Control.
answers.evidence: “first dead Character: all Escape Pods are automatically Unlocked”; “For the rest of the game they may be Locked/Unlocked normally.”

requested_parts: What does the Storage Room's Search for an Item Room Action let you draw and keep, where exactly does the rejected card go, and what are the common Room Action cost and restrictions?
answers.answer: 1) Storage Action draws 2 from chosen Red/Yellow/Green deck, keeps one and returns other face down to bottom of chosen deck. 2) Costs 2 cards and normal Room rules: in Room, out of Combat, no Malfunction. Unlike ordinary Search, Storage works repeatedly at zero counter; ordinary Search decrements counter and stops at zero.
answers.evidence: “Storage — draw 2 cards from a chosen Item deck ... keep 1, other to the bottom”; “Cost: 2 Action cards”; “works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero”; “counter limits only the Search Action card.”

requested_parts: While in the Nest, how do you take an Egg still represented on the Intruder board, what does that Action cost, and what happens immediately afterward? How does this differ from picking up a previously dropped Egg token in your Room?
answers.answer: 1) Nest Room Action costs 2 cards; take one Egg token from Intruder board then make Noise roll. 2) A dropped Egg token is a Heavy Object: pick it up with Basic Action cost 1, with no prescribed Noise roll.
answers.evidence: “Nest — take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board, then make a Noise roll”; “Room Actions ... Cost: 2 Action cards”; “Pick Up Heavy Object (cost 1 Action card)”; “This Basic pickup has no Noise-roll instruction.”

requested_parts: You perform the Action printed on a One Use Only Item. Besides paying its Action-card cost and showing it, what happens to the Item card after use?
answers.answer: 1) After paying cost and showing Item, discard One Use Only Item card after use.
answers.evidence: “One Use Only means discard that Item after its effect, in addition to paying its Action-card cost”; “Any Item used must be shown to all players.”

requested_parts: For a rule concerned with the Character's arrival on Earth, where is a Character in a launched Escape Pod treated as having arrived? Does this establish that the ship itself reached Earth?
answers.answer: 1) A launched Pod occupant counts as having arrived on Earth. 2) This does not establish that the ship reached Earth; Pod arrival is separate from ship Coordinates/jump result.
answers.evidence: “occupants’ miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth”; ship arrival is checked by “reveal the Coordinates card and read the destination selected.”

requested_parts: While waiting in an Escape Pod, must you roll Noise when Adult bag development calls for it?
answers.answer: 1) Yes. While waiting, you are treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development, so roll when Adult development calls all players to roll (unless otherwise excluded; summary says waiters count present).
answers.evidence: “You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development.”

requested_parts: A Malfunction is placed in the Evacuation Section while you are already waiting in its Pod. Can you launch, wait or exit, and what does that Malfunction prevent?
answers.answer: 1) Yes, may remain waiting, launch, or exit; Malfunction blocks only new entry to Pods.
answers.evidence: “you may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new entry to Pods.”

requested_parts: When Escaping from several differently sized Intruders, how many attacks and in what order?
answers.answer: 1) Resolve one separate Escape attack per Intruder, largest to smallest: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva.
answers.evidence: “one separate Attack per Intruder ... starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva).”

requested_parts: An Event instructs removing itself from the game but its other effect cannot be resolved. Is it removed?
answers.answer: 1) Yes, remove the Event if it instructs removal even if its other effect cannot resolve.
answers.evidence: “Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve.”

requested_parts: When Adult bag development triggers Noise, when does the drawn Adult token return, and may a triggered Encounter draw that very token?
answers.answer: 1) Adult token is returned immediately before all players’ Noise rolls. 2) An Encounter triggered by those rolls may draw the very same Adult.
answers.evidence: “return the token to the bag immediately before all players roll for Noise”; “An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token.”

requested_parts: A retreating Intruder meets a Closed Door. What happens normally, and what changes under The Way of Moving Weakness for an affected non-Breeder/non-Queen?
answers.answer: 1) Normally a retreating Intruder meeting Closed Door destroys it and stays. 2) With The Way of Moving, affected Intruder other than Breeder/Queen does nothing at that Door.
answers.evidence: “A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays”; “with The Way of Moving ... other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door.”

requested_parts: Does the Hand Serious Wound increase the cost of Basic Shoot, and why?
answers.answer: 1) No. Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost because Shoot is Basic Action, not Item Action.
answers.evidence: “does not increase Basic Shoot cost because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.”

requested_parts: With Vulnerability to Fire discovered, how much extra Injury applies per damage instance, and how many Injuries for a Flamethrower double-crosshair hit?
answers.answer: 1) Vulnerability to Fire adds one Injury per damage instance (x+1), not for each injury in the instance; Flamethrower double-crosshair hit deals 3 injuries.
answers.evidence: “1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury”; “Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries.”

requested_parts: A Larva attacks a Character who already has a Larva on their board. What happens to each Larva and to the Character?
answers.answer: 1) Attacking Larva disappears; existing Larva remains. Character gains one Contamination card and is not automatically killed.
answers.evidence: “attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them.”

requested_parts: After a Character hibernates, Fire appears in the Hibernatorium. Does the sleeper take Fire wounds and what can still kill them?
answers.answer: 1) Hibernating Character does not take later Fire wounds. 2) Ship destruction can still kill them; final survival/Contamination/Objectives checks also apply.
answers.evidence: “A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium”; “ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter.”

requested_parts: Can the Coolant Leak Event start Self-Destruct while someone hibernates, and how does that differ from starting it as a Character?
answers.answer: 1) Yes, Coolant Leak Event may start Self-Destruct with sleeper present; Character cannot start it while anyone hibernates.
answers.evidence: “Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating; the Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers.”

requested_parts: Where do discarded/dead Intruder tokens go, and can they be reused later?
answers.answer: 1) Discarded/dead Intruder tokens go to unused token pool, not permanent removal, and can be reused.
answers.evidence: “Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently.”

requested_parts: Can Fire and Malfunction markers be placed in unexplored Rooms?
answers.answer: 1) Fire may be placed in unexplored Rooms; Malfunction may not.
answers.evidence: “Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can.”

requested_parts: A Character with two Light Wounds receives two more Light Wounds. What Wounds remain after resolving them?
answers.answer: 1) First extra Light Wound converts two Lights to one Serious Wound; the second extra Light Wound remains as one Light Wound. Result: 1 Serious + 1 Light.
answers.evidence: “Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound.”

requested_parts: On a Character death in standard play, what happens to Heavy Objects versus their Item cards?
answers.answer: 1) On death Heavy Objects drop in Room; Item cards disappear from game.
answers.evidence: “Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game.”

requested_parts: Self-Destruct reaches its first yellow space, Pods unlock, then are relocked. Does reaching the next yellow space unlock them again?
answers.answer: 1) No. First yellow unlocks; subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock Pods again, even if relocked.
answers.evidence: “subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again.”

requested_parts: Does destroying the ship fulfill Objectives to kill the Queen or destroy the Nest; does that alone make your Character a winner?
answers.answer: 1) Ship destruction fulfills requirements to kill Queen/destroy Nest. 2) Character must still survive and fulfill own Objective to win.
answers.evidence: “Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements”; “your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective.”

requested_parts: May you intentionally spend an empty Trade Action with no intention of exchange; what if honest negotiations end without a trade?
answers.answer: 1) No, empty Trade with no meaningful change/intention should be disallowed. 2) Genuine negotiations may end without trade.
answers.evidence: “Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention”; “Honest negotiations may end with no trade.”

requested_parts: What kind of Action activates a Quest Item, may it be done in Combat, and does a Room Malfunction prevent it?
answers.answer: 1) Quest activation is a Basic Action, out of Combat. 2) Malfunction does not prevent activation.
answers.evidence: “Quest activation is a Basic Action ... forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room.”

requested_parts: Which Basic Actions can be used in Combat; can you Trade, Craft or Pick Up an Object there? What about permitted card or Item Actions?
answers.answer: 1) Combat Basic Actions: Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape. Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object and Quest activation prohibited. 2) Card/Item Actions with no restriction or In Combat marking may be used if their own requirements allow; Room Actions are prohibited.
answers.evidence: “Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape”; “no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object or Quest Item activation”; “Room Actions remain forbidden”; unmarked actions “may use it in either situation.”

requested_parts: Can Soldier use Covering Fire only on themselves, and how are direction, Noise and Surprise targeting handled when moving two Characters?
answers.answer: 1) Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. 2) Both move in direction of their choice, then one Noise roll; Encounter Surprise check is against Soldier.
answers.evidence: “Soldier may use it for themselves alone”; “Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll”; “Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier.”

requested_parts: How does Full Auto calculate damage and consume Ammo?
answers.answer: 1) Discard all Assault Rifle Ammo and perform one Shoot; extra damage equals half discarded Ammo rounded down, plus Assault Rifle +1 and the Shoot die result.
answers.evidence: “remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle’s +1 bonus.”

requested_parts: When can Nerves of Steel be chosen relative to seeing the Attack card, and may it protect you when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack?
answers.answer: 1) Soldier may see Intruder Attack card before choosing Nerves of Steel. 2) It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still receive effects such as Frenzy.
answers.evidence: “you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it”; “can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement or Reconnaissance reveals a Danger/Silence Exploration token. Does that automatic result apply or the movement ability?
answers.answer: 1) Careful Movement replaces automatic Silence/Danger with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels automatic results too.
answers.evidence: “Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.”

requested_parts: May Captain use Order while personally in Combat; may Intercom force someone else to Move out of Combat and what rules apply?
answers.answer: 1) Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. 2) Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat; normal Escape rules apply.
answers.evidence: “Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat”; “Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape.”

requested_parts: Who can draw an Action card when Captain uses Motivation with active Intercom?
answers.answer: 1) Motivation with active Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room.
answers.evidence: “Motivation with Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room.”

requested_parts: Moving via Technical Corridors card or Plans Item reveals a Door Exploration token. Where does the Door go?
answers.answer: 1) Ignore the Door Exploration token because entry Corridor cannot be determined when entering by Technical Corridors Action or Plans.
answers.evidence: “Entering via Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined.”

requested_parts: Can you Interrupt a Captain Order played remotely via Intercom when you are not in the Captain Room; does passing bar playing Interruption?
answers.answer: 1) Cannot Interrupt remote Order via Intercom from elsewhere; Interruption requires same Room as Character performing interrupted Action. 2) Passing does not bar Interruption, subject to requirements.
answers.evidence: “Interruption ... requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere”; “may still play Interruption after passing.”

requested_parts: After two Actions your hand is empty. Do you automatically pass then, and what timing consequence can Fire or Bleeding have?
answers.answer: 1) No automatic pass when hand empties after two Actions; wait until next round to pass. 2) That extra round may incur another Fire or Bleeding effect.
answers.evidence: “empty hand does not automatically make you pass after completing 2 Actions. Wait for your next round to pass; that extra round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect.”

requested_parts: Rest scans several Infected cards while no Larva was on your board. Can the scan kill you from multiple infected cards; when can Rest be fatal?
answers.answer: 1) No: if no Larva before Rest, multiple infected scanned cards place only one Larva and cannot kill via multiples alone. 2) Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on board before it.
answers.evidence: “Rest with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva”; “Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it.”

requested_parts: You throw a Grenade/Molotov at uncarried Eggs in the Nest from a neighboring Room. Where is the required Noise roll resolved?
answers.answer: 1) Resolve required Noise roll in your own Room, not Nest.
answers.evidence: “Throwing a Grenade/Molotov at Nest Eggs from another Room makes you roll Noise in your own Room, not the Nest.”

requested_parts: Scientist uses Intranet to research an Object while carrying it outside the Laboratory. Can that reveal a Weakness?
answers.answer: 1) No. Object itself must be in Laboratory even if Scientist uses Intranet from elsewhere; otherwise it cannot reveal Weakness.
answers.evidence: “Intranet research still requires the Object itself in the Laboratory, regardless of Scientist’s location.”

requested_parts: Storage Item Counter is zero. Can you use its Room Action repeatedly, and how is ordinary Search different?
answers.answer: 1) Yes, Storage Room Action can be used repeatedly at zero counter, paying normal cost/restrictions. 2) Its counter limits only Search Action card; ordinary Search decrements and is unavailable at zero.
answers.evidence: “Storage’s Room Action works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero”; “Its counter limits only the Search Action card.”

requested_parts: When the Nest is on Fire and Vulnerability to Fire is discovered, how many of its Eggs are destroyed each Fire Damage step?
answers.answer: 1) Two Eggs from Nest pool are destroyed each Event Fire Damage step with Vulnerability to Fire.
answers.evidence: “Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness.”

requested_parts: Take an Egg from the Intruder board and drop it back in the Nest Room. Does it restore the Nest Egg total for destruction purposes?
answers.answer: 1) No. Returned Egg is a normal Heavy Object and does not restore Nest Egg total/hit points.
answers.evidence: “An Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest is a normal Heavy Object and does not restore the Nest’s Egg total/hit points.”

requested_parts: Smoke Grenade says each target loses one Action card. Who chooses and where does it go?
answers.answer: 1) Each affected player chooses one Action card from their hand and discards it to their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: “Smoke Grenade’s affected player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their hand.”

requested_parts: Can Medkit and Bandages be used on other Characters?
answers.answer: 1) Yes, Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.
answers.evidence: “Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters.”

requested_parts: May you use your Energy Charge directly to reload another Character Weapon; what procedure permits that recharge?
answers.answer: 1) No direct use on another Character’s Weapon. Trade the Energy Charge to them so they can use it in their own round.
answers.evidence: “Energy Charge cannot directly reload another Character’s Weapon: trade them the Charge so they use it in their own round.”

requested_parts: Alcohol scans an Infected Contamination card. Does this place a Larva and what happens instead?
answers.answer: 1) Alcohol’s Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card.
answers.evidence: “Alcohol’s Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card.”

requested_parts: Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to an already-used or empty Energy Weapon: does it immediately provide extra Ammo?
answers.answer: 1) Yes. Attaching Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo.
answers.evidence: “Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo.”

requested_parts: When you Craft a Flamethrower, does it start fully loaded or with the one Ammo of a searched Weapon?
answers.answer: 1) Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, not with one Ammo.
answers.evidence: “A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, rather than the one Ammo of a searched Weapon.”

requested_parts: Does the Hand Serious Wound affect Scout Motion Scanner and why?
answers.answer: 1) No. Hand Serious Wound does not affect Scout’s Motion Scanner because it is a unique reaction, not an Item Action.
answers.evidence: “It also does not affect Scout’s Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action.”

requested_parts: Describe Antidote: scan scope, removed cards, new Contamination, reshuffling, hand retention and passing; how does Surgery differ?
answers.answer: 1) Antidote scans all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; removes all Infected and Larva if present; gain one new Contamination; reshuffle new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in hand; then pass, may keep hand. 2) Surgery also removes Larva but scans all zones, shuffles entire hand, gives no new card, costs 1 Light Wound and auto-passes.
answers.evidence: “scan all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard”; “remove all Infected cards ... and remove a Larva”; “Gain 1 new Contamination card”; “except cards retained in your hand. Then pass; you may keep hand cards”; “Surgery ... shuffles the entire hand too, gives no new ... and costs 1 Light Wound.”

requested_parts: On exploration, where are Slime, Fire, Malfunction and Door effects placed, and which Corridor receives the Door?
answers.answer: 1) Exploration Slime goes on Character board; Fire/Malfunction marker placed in entered Room; Door token placed in Corridor by which entered. Malfunction cannot be placed unexplored; Fire can.
answers.evidence: “Slime — place a Slime ... marker on your Character board”; “Fire — place a Fire marker in this Room”; “Malfunction — place ... in this Room”; “Doors — place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered”; “Malfunction ... unexplored ... whereas Fire markers can.”

requested_parts: During the Event Phase Fire Damage step, how many Injuries does each Intruder in a burning Room take, when relative to attacks, and does it trigger an Injury Effect check?
answers.answer: 1) Each Intruder in burning Room suffers one Injury in Fire Damage step, after Intruder Attacks and before Event card; immediately perform normal Injury Effect check, including death/retreat.
answers.evidence: “each Intruder in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Injury”; “after Intruder Attacks and before the Event card”; “Apply Injury markers and the normal Injury Effect check immediately.”

requested_parts: Can you perform any Search Action in the Nest or Room Covered With Slime, even though ordinary Room tiles usually permit searching?
answers.answer: 1) No. Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit any Search Action; ordinary Search permissions do not override.
answers.evidence: “The Nest and Room Covered With Slime explicitly prohibit any Search Action.”

requested_parts: An Intruder is in a neighboring Room, but the connecting Corridor has a Closed Door. May you throw a Grenade into that Room through that Corridor?
answers.answer: 1) No. Closed Door blocks Grenade throws through that Corridor.
answers.evidence: “Closed ... blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws).”

requested_parts: A Noise marker was placed on the basic board's Technical Corridors space because of a roll in one Room. Later, a Character in a distant Room rolls the number of a different Technical Corridors Entrance: is that entrance already noisy? Also, can a Closed Door make an ordinary Corridor's Noise marker apply only on the other side of that Door?
answers.answer: 1) Yes, Technical Corridors noise is shared: one marker is treated as present at every Entrance, so different Entrance roll meets existing marker/Encounter. 2) Ordinary Corridor marker applies to whole Corridor; Door never restricts noise to one side.
answers.evidence: “A Noise marker there is treated as if it were in every Technical Corridors Entrance”; “Noise markers ... never affect ... Doors”; “marker in a Corridor with a Closed Door still affects the WHOLE Corridor.”

requested_parts: Outside Combat, what can a single use of Bandages do to Wounds, and what two alternatives does Clothes offer? Can Bandages heal an undressed Serious Wound directly? Give each Item's Action-card cost and whether its alternatives can be combined in one use.
answers.answer: 1) Bandages cost 1, One Use Only, out of Combat; choose Dress one Serious Wound OR Heal all Light Wounds. Cannot heal undressed Serious Wound directly. 2) Clothes costs 1, One Use Only, out of Combat; choose discard Slime OR Dress one Serious Wound. Alternatives are exclusive, not combined.
answers.evidence: “Bandages ... 1; One Use Only ... Out of Combat only ... Dress 1 Serious Wound OR Heal all Light Wounds”; “Clothes ... Discard your Slime marker OR Dress 1 Serious Wound”; “Choose only one effect when a card gives alternatives”; dressing “does not Heal or discard a Serious Wound.”

requested_parts: What can the Fire Extinguisher Item do in one use: which Room or Intruder may it affect, can it both extinguish Fire and force Retreat, and what does it cost?
answers.answer: 1) Fire Extinguisher costs 1, One Use Only and may be used in Combat. Choose either discard Fire from your current Room or force one Intruder in your current Room to Retreat. Cannot combine effects.
answers.evidence: “Fire Extinguisher ... 1; One Use Only”; “May be used in Combat”; “Discard Fire from your current Room OR choose 1 Intruder in your current Room and force it to Retreat”; “does not combine both effects.”

requested_parts: What are the Taser Item's two alternative effects and their legal target location? If you choose its Character-targeting effect, is just one Action card lost, or what exactly is discarded?
answers.answer: 1) Taser costs 1, One Use Only, usable in Combat; choose one Intruder in your Room to take 1 Injury and Retreat OR one Character in your Room to discard all cards in their hand. 2) The Character loses all hand cards, including Contamination, not merely one.
answers.evidence: “Taser ... Choose 1 Intruder in your Room: it suffers 1 Injury and Retreats. OR choose 1 Character ... discard all cards in your hand, including Contamination cards.”

requested_parts: With no Weakness modifying damage, you shoot a Queen using a Flamethrower. What happens on a small curled Intruder-symbol result, on the blank miss face, and on the two-crosshair face? Include any Fire placement.
answers.answer: 1) Small curled symbol ordinarily misses Queen, but Flamethrower always deals at least 1 Injury except blank miss, so Queen gets 1. 2) Blank is miss, no Injury. 3) Two crosshairs gives 2 Injuries and places Fire marker in shooter’s Room.
answers.evidence: “Flamethrower ... always deals at least 1 Injury except on the blank miss face, even if ... Intruder symbol would normally miss”; “two-crosshair result deals ... 2 Injuries and also places a Fire marker in your Room.”

requested_parts: What Room may a Molotov Cocktail target, and what does it do immediately to Fire, Intruders and Characters there? If you use it in your own Room, does its immediate damage exclude you?
answers.answer: 1) Molotov targets own Room or neighboring Room containing Intruder; uncarried Eggs also make target legal. It places Fire; immediately each Intruder takes 1 Injury and each Character there takes 1 Serious Wound. 2) Yes, includes you if present.
answers.evidence: “Choose your Room or a neighboring Room containing an Intruder (uncarried Eggs also permit the target)”; “Place Fire there; immediately, each Intruder suffers 1 Injury and each Character suffers 1 Serious Wound, including you if you are there.”

requested_parts: When you use your own Energy Charge, how much Ammo may it restore and to what type of Weapon? What alternative Door effect can you choose, and which Doors are in range?
answers.answer: 1) Energy Charge costs 1, One Use Only; fully loads one of your own Energy Weapons up to capacity. 2) Alternative is open or close one Door in Corridor connected to your Room; cannot close Destroyed Door.
answers.evidence: “Fully load 1 of your own Energy Weapons (up to its Ammo capacity) OR Open or Close 1 Door in a Corridor connected to your Room”; “normal prohibition on closing Destroyed Doors applies.”

requested_parts: Where and at what Action-card cost do you activate the Pilot's Evacuation Key? Once active, where must you be to use it, what can it do to Pods, and is it a reusable remote substitute for Hatch Control System?
answers.answer: 1) Activate Pilot’s Evacuation Key with cost-1 Basic Action, out of Combat, in Fire Control System. 2) Once active, cost-1 use in Evacuation Section Room locks/unlocks one Pod in that Section; One Use Only. 3) Not remote or reusable substitute for Hatch Control.
answers.evidence: “Each activation ... cost-1 Basic Action, out of Combat”; “Pilot’s Evacuation Key | Fire Control System Room | In an Evacuation Section Room, Lock or Unlock 1 Pod in that Section. One Use Only ... neither remote nor reusable.”

requested_parts: Where and at what cost is the Captain's Log Key activated, and how is the activated Item used to inspect another player's secret Objectives? Must that other Character share your Room?
answers.answer: 1) Activate Captain’s Log Key with cost-1 Basic Action, out of Combat, in Comms Room. 2) Active Item costs 1 in a Room with available Computer; inspect chosen player’s retained Objectives. Target need not share room; one-use.
answers.evidence: “Captain’s Log Key | Comms Room”; “In a Room with an available Computer, look at the retained Objective cards of a chosen player; their Character need not share your Room”; “Each activation ... cost-1 Basic Action”; “One Use Only.”

requested_parts: What does the Six Shooter card require for reloading, and how many Injuries does its single-crosshair Combat die result deal when no Weakness changes damage?
answers.answer: 1) Six Shooter reload requires Reload Action card. 2) Single-crosshair result deals 1 additional Injury, i.e. 2 total before other modifiers.
answers.evidence: “Six Shooter ... can only be reloaded with a Reload Action card, and a single-crosshair result deals 1 additional Injury (2 total before other modifiers).”

requested_parts: The Captain plays Suppressive Fire, whose printed Action cost is 0. Must any Ammo still be spent? Does it move both the Captain and another Character, or one selected Character; must that other Character agree, and are the normal Escape attacks resolved?
answers.answer: 1) Suppressive Fire cost 0 Action cards beyond using card, but still discard 1 Ammo. 2) Move yourself OR one other Character in your Room, not both; other Character must agree. 3) No normal Escape attack triggered.
answers.evidence: “Suppressive Fire | 0”; “Discard 1 Ammo, then move yourself OR 1 other Character in your Room, with that player’s agreement”; “one selected Character, not both”; “does not trigger an Intruder Attack.”

requested_parts: When you use Nemesis Plans, how many unexplored Room tiles may you check, may you also inspect their Exploration tokens as with Monitoring Room, and what are the Item's Action-card cost and use restrictions?
answers.answer: 1) Nemesis Plans checks any two unexplored tiles privately and returns them face down; does not inspect Exploration tokens. 2) Costs 1 card, One Use Only, Out of Combat only.
answers.evidence: “Privately check any 2 unexplored Room tiles, then return them face down. Do not inspect their Exploration tokens”; “Nemesis Plans | 1; One Use Only”; “Out of Combat only.”

requested_parts: With no Weakness modifying damage, you Shoot an Intruder using the Scientist's Pistol and roll the two-crosshair result. How many Injuries do you place, and do you still check the Injury Effect?
answers.answer: 1) Scientist’s Pistol changes two-crosshair result to one Injury. 2) Still conduct normal Injury Effect check.
answers.evidence: “Scientist’s Pistol treats a two-crosshair result as only 1 Injury, followed by the normal Injury Effect check.”

requested_parts: After every player has had one round of two Actions, does the Event Phase begin automatically? Describe who takes the next round, the order and size of rounds while players remain active, what happens when a player takes only one Action or none, and exactly when the Player Phase ends.
answers.answer: 1) No automatic Event Phase after each player’s first round; repeat rounds while anyone has not passed, in First Player order, with two Actions per round. 2) One Action requires passing; choosing/cannot do none means pass. After passing no normal Actions but Interruption allowed. Empty hand after 2 Actions does not force immediate pass; next round pass may incur Fire/Bleeding. 3) Player Phase ends when all players passed; then Event Phase.
answers.evidence: “Series of rounds repeat as long as at least one player has not passed”; “each player performs a round of 2 Actions”; “If you perform only 1 Action ... you must pass”; “If ... choose not to, you must pass”; “all players passed”; “empty hand does not automatically make you pass after completing 2 Actions.”

requested_parts: When you use Canteen or Shower, what non-scanning benefit does each Room give? Must you choose between that benefit and scanning Contamination, or can one Room Action give both? May you take the non-scanning benefit without choosing to scan?
answers.answer: 1) Canteen heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes Slime. 2) Each may also scan all hand Contamination and remove non-Infected, so one Room Action provides both benefit and scan. 3) “may also” means non-scanning benefit may be taken without scanning.
answers.evidence: “Canteen — Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND”; “Shower Room — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan”; “may also”

requested_parts: Before a Contamination card has been Scanned, is its INFECTED/not-INFECTED status known to its player? When an effect instructs a Scan, how is that status read, and does a coded word merely resembling INFECTED count?
answers.answer: 1) Unscanned status remains unknown; player cannot know INFECTED/not-Infected until Scanner reveals coded text. 2) Scan by overlaying red foil; exact word INFECTED appearing in one line means infected; absence means not infected. Merely similar-looking coded word does not count.
answers.evidence: “Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner”; “place the Scanner’s red foil over the card’s coded text field”; “If the exact word INFECTED appears in one line”; “A merely similar-looking coded word does not count.”
